description: Recurring frustrations people hit while pursuing leisure hobbies: video and board gaming, playing music, fiber and paper crafts, gardening, DIY projects, reading, and collecting.

items.title: Forgetting which video games you already own
items.problem: Games are spread across Steam, Epic, GOG, PlayStation, Xbox, Switch and old physical discs, so people buy a game they already got free or bundled years ago.
items.who: PC and console gamers with libraries on multiple storefronts
items.workaround: Manually searching each launcher before buying; spreadsheets

items.title: Huge backlog of unplayed games
items.problem: Sales and subscriptions pile up hundreds of unplayed titles, and people freeze trying to pick what to play next, then buy more instead of playing what they own.
items.who: Gamers who buy during Steam sales or use Game Pass
items.workaround: Spreadsheets, Backloggd, random-picker sites

items.title: Returning to a game after months away
items.problem: Picking a story game back up after a long break means having no idea what the plot was, what the controls do, or what quest was in progress.
items.who: Adult gamers who play in bursts
items.workaround: Watching recap videos on YouTube or restarting from scratch

items.title: Coordinating a raid or group session night
items.problem: Getting five to twenty adults with jobs and kids online at the same time across time zones takes days of Discord back-and-forth, and one no-show cancels the night.
items.who: Guild and clan members in MMOs and co-op games
items.workaround: Discord polls, Google Sheets sign-ups, Raid-Helper bots

items.title: Tracking which game subscription has which title
items.problem: Titles rotate on and off Game Pass, PS Plus, and Netflix Games, so people miss a game leaving the catalog mid-playthrough or pay for a game that was included.
items.workaround: Checking monthly 'leaving soon' blog posts

items.title: Waiting for a wishlisted game's price drop
items.problem: People watch wishlists across several stores and still miss the historic-low sale on a game they wanted, or buy right before it goes on sale.
items.workaround: IsThereAnyDeal, Steam wishlist emails, Deku Deals

items.title: Losing track of achievements and completion goals
items.problem: Completionists forget which collectibles, side quests or achievements they have left in a large open-world game and end up re-checking wikis constantly.
items.workaround: Wiki checklists, printed guides, spreadsheets

items.title: Screen-time limits that kill a game session
items.problem: Parents and gamers themselves want to cap play, but hard cutoffs mid-match cause rage-quits, penalties in ranked modes, and family fights.
items.who: Parents of gaming kids; adults trying to limit play
items.workaround: Console parental controls, kitchen timers, arguments

items.title: Sharing game clips across platforms
items.problem: Clips captured on PS5, Xbox or Switch are stuck in each platform's ecosystem, and getting them to a phone or Discord takes several steps and quality loss.
items.who: Console gamers who share highlights with friends
items.workaround: Uploading to Twitter/YouTube then re-downloading; USB drives

items.title: Not knowing what to practice today
items.problem: Amateur musicians sit down with the instrument and noodle through the same songs for twenty minutes without structure, then feel they did not improve.
items.who: Self-taught guitar, piano and other instrument learners
items.workaround: YouTube lessons, paper practice plans, teachers

items.title: Losing a practice streak and quitting
items.problem: Practice logs live in a notebook or memory, so progress is invisible and motivation collapses after a busy week with no sessions.
items.workaround: Habit-tracker apps, paper calendars

items.title: Finding accurate chords or tabs for a song
items.problem: Tab and chord sites are full of wrong versions, transposed keys, popups and paywalls, so players waste time verifying by ear which version is right.
items.who: Guitarists, ukulele and piano players learning songs
items.workaround: Comparing multiple versions on Ultimate Guitar; slowing down YouTube

items.title: Slowing down a song section to learn it
items.problem: Learning a solo or riff requires looping a few seconds at half speed without pitch change, and juggling a phone, a DAW and sheet music is clumsy.
items.workaround: YouTube speed settings, Transcribe!, Anytune

items.title: Managing a band's shared setlist and lyrics
items.problem: Band members keep different versions of the setlist, keys and lyrics on paper and in group chats, leading to on-stage confusion about which key or arrangement was agreed.
items.who: Amateur bands and church worship teams
items.workaround: Google Docs, printed binders, WhatsApp threads

items.title: Finding people to jam with nearby
items.problem: Hobby musicians struggle to find others of similar skill, taste and schedule in their area, and Craigslist-style ads attract flakes.
items.workaround: Facebook groups, music store bulletin boards, open mics

items.title: Organizing hundreds of PDF sheet music files
items.problem: Sheet music is scattered across downloads folders, email attachments and photos, with no way to find a piece by composer, key or difficulty when it is needed.
items.workaround: forScore, folders, binders

items.title: Turning pages while both hands play
items.problem: Reading a long piece from a tablet or paper means stopping to flip pages mid-phrase unless someone is there to turn them.
items.workaround: Bluetooth foot pedals, memorizing, photocopies taped together

items.title: Losing your place in a knitting pattern
items.problem: Knitters and crocheters lose count of rows and repeats when interrupted, then have to rip back hours of work after discovering the mistake.
items.workaround: Row counters, tally marks, sticky notes on the pattern

items.title: Yarn stash nobody can inventory
items.problem: Crafters forget what yarn they own, in what weight and yardage, and buy duplicates or run short mid-project because they cannot check the stash from the store.
items.workaround: Ravelry stash pages, spreadsheets, bins with labels

items.title: Too many works in progress abandoned
items.problem: Half-finished projects pile up in bags, and crafters forget which needles, yarn and pattern belong to which one, so nothing ever gets completed.
items.workaround: Project bags, Ravelry project pages, guilt

items.title: Calculating fabric or yarn needed for a size
items.problem: Adjusting a pattern for a different size or gauge requires math many crafters get wrong, leading to running out of material or wasted purchases.
items.workaround: Calculator and scrap paper, buying extra

items.title: Pricing handmade items for sale
items.problem: Makers who sell at craft fairs or Etsy underprice because they do not track material cost and hours per item and feel awkward charging for labor.
items.workaround: Rules of thumb, spreadsheets, guessing

items.title: Craft supply hoard with unknown contents
items.problem: Beads, paper, paint, fabric scraps and tools fill drawers, and people rebuy items they already own because nothing is catalogued or findable.
items.workaround: Clear bins, labels, occasional purges

items.title: Cross-stitch chart tracking on paper
items.problem: Following a large multi-color chart on paper means highlighting stitched areas by hand and losing the place when the printout gets folded or lost.
items.workaround: Highlighter pens, Pattern Keeper app, magnet boards

items.title: Forgetting when to water each plant
items.problem: Houseplant owners over- or under-water because every plant has different needs and they cannot remember when they last watered which one.
items.who: Houseplant owners with more than a handful of plants
items.workaround: Finger test, reminder apps like Planta, watering on a fixed day

items.title: Missing the sowing window for vegetables
items.problem: Gardeners realize in June they should have started tomatoes indoors in March, because seed timing depends on local frost dates that packets do not know.
items.workaround: Almanac charts, seed packet math, spreadsheets

items.title: Identifying a pest or disease on a plant
items.problem: Yellow leaves or spots could be dozens of things, and searching images gives contradictory advice while the plant declines.
items.workaround: Facebook groups, extension office, guessing

items.title: Forgetting what was planted where
items.problem: By midsummer the plant labels have faded or blown away and gardeners cannot tell which tomato variety is which, so they cannot repeat successes next year.
items.workaround: Paper garden journals, photos, plastic labels

items.title: Planning crop rotation between seasons
items.problem: Rotating plant families across beds each year to avoid disease requires remembering last year's layout, which nobody wrote down.
items.workaround: Graph paper sketches, memory

items.title: Seed packets expiring unnoticed
items.problem: Half-used seed packets accumulate for years and gardeners sow old seed that fails to germinate, wasting a season's slot.
items.workaround: Shoebox sorting, germination tests

items.title: Frost warning missed overnight
items.problem: A surprise late frost kills seedlings because weather apps do not warn at the garden's microclimate level or in time to cover plants.
items.workaround: Checking forecasts nightly in spring, row covers

items.title: Glut of harvest with nowhere to go
items.problem: Zucchini and tomatoes all ripen at once and gardeners cannot use, preserve or give away enough before it rots.
items.workaround: Leaving bags on neighbors' porches, canning marathons

items.title: Half-finished DIY projects around the house
items.problem: A weekend project stalls for months because the next step needs one part or one dry day, and by then the plan and measurements are forgotten.
items.who: Homeowners doing their own repairs and builds
items.workaround: Notes app, nagging from partner

items.title: Multiple trips to the hardware store
items.problem: DIYers go to the store three times per project because the cut list or fastener count was estimated from memory and something was missed.
items.workaround: Handwritten lists, buying extra of everything

items.title: Optimizing board cuts to reduce waste
items.problem: Figuring out how to cut a plywood sheet or lumber into needed pieces with minimal offcuts is error-prone on paper, and mistakes waste expensive material.
items.workaround: Graph paper, online cut optimizers

items.title: Forgetting paint colors and finishes used
items.problem: Touching up a wall years later fails because nobody remembers the exact paint brand, color code and sheen, and the leftover can has dried out.
items.workaround: Writing on the can, photos of the lid, guessing at the store

items.title: Tool inventory and lending loss
items.problem: Tools lent to neighbors or friends never come back, and owners cannot remember who has the drill or the ladder.
items.workaround: Memory, asking around

items.title: Saving project inspiration that is findable later
items.problem: Ideas from Pinterest, YouTube and Instagram get saved in five places, and when it is time to build the bookshelf nobody can find the video with the joinery detail.
items.workaround: Pinterest boards, browser bookmarks, screenshots

items.title: Tracking 3D printer filament and settings
items.problem: 3D printing hobbyists forget which filament spool has how much left and which temperature settings worked for it, leading to failed prints and mid-print run-outs.
items.workaround: Spreadsheets, weighing spools, notes on the spool

items.title: Ever-growing to-be-read pile
items.problem: Readers keep buying and borrowing books faster than they read them and feel guilt and choice paralysis choosing the next one.
items.workaround: Goodreads shelves, StoryGraph, notebooks

items.title: Forgetting what happened in the previous book
items.problem: When the next book in a series comes out a year later, readers cannot remember characters and plot and either reread or read confused.
items.who: Fantasy, sci-fi and mystery series readers
items.workaround: Fan wikis, 'recaptains' sites, rereading

items.title: Tracking reading order across a series
items.problem: Series with novellas, prequels and spin-offs have confusing reading orders, and readers accidentally read book four before book three.
items.workaround: Author websites, fan-made reading order lists

items.title: Library holds returning all at once
items.problem: Library ebook holds placed months apart all become available in the same week, and readers cannot finish them before the loan expires and the queue restarts.
items.workaround: Suspending holds manually, panic reading

items.title: Book club scheduling and picking a book
items.problem: Book clubs stall on picking the next title and finding a date everyone can make, with debates dragging on in group chats.
items.workaround: Group chat polls, one person deciding

items.title: Highlights and notes lost across formats
items.problem: Notes taken in a Kindle, a physical book and an audiobook never end up in one place, so readers cannot find the quote they remember.
items.workaround: Readwise, photos of pages, sticky tabs

items.title: Lending books and never getting them back
items.problem: Readers lend books to friends and forget who has what, and the book disappears permanently.
items.workaround: Memory, a sticky note on the shelf

items.title: Board game night scheduling and headcount
items.problem: Game night depends on knowing exactly how many people are coming, because most games have hard player counts, and last-minute drops leave a five-player game with three.
items.workaround: Group chats, Doodle, guessing

items.title: Choosing a game for the group tonight
items.problem: With a shelf of fifty games, hosts struggle to pick one that fits the player count, time available and the mix of newbies and veterans present.
items.workaround: BoardGameGeek collection filters, arguing

items.title: Re-teaching rules after months
items.problem: Nobody remembers the rules of a game played once last year, and reading the rulebook aloud kills thirty minutes of the evening.
items.workaround: YouTube how-to-play videos, player-aid cards

items.title: Scorekeeping for complex games
items.problem: End-game scoring in heavy euros involves many categories and errors are common, and score sheets run out or get lost.
items.workaround: Paper pads, phone calculators, official companion apps

items.title: Tracking who won which games over time
items.problem: Groups want to know play counts, win rates and streaks for bragging rights but have no record of past plays.
items.workaround: BG Stats app, spreadsheets, memory

items.title: Missing pieces discovered mid-game
items.problem: A game is set up before anyone realizes a card or token is missing, and finding the publisher's replacement-parts form takes ages.
items.who: Board game owners, especially secondhand buyers
items.workaround: Improvising with coins, publisher parts requests

items.title: Running a tabletop RPG campaign's notes
items.problem: Game masters juggle NPC names, plot threads, maps and player backstories across notebooks and Google Docs, and players forget what happened last session.
items.who: Dungeons & Dragons and other TTRPG groups
items.workaround: Obsidian vaults, World Anvil, binders

items.title: Finding a consistent D&D session time
items.problem: The most common reason campaigns die is that four to six adults cannot find a recurring slot, and every session requires renegotiation.
items.workaround: When2meet, Discord polls, giving up

items.title: Not knowing a collection's total value
items.problem: Collectors of cards, coins, vinyl or figures have no idea what their collection is worth for insurance or sale, and prices shift constantly.
items.workaround: Spreadsheets with manual price lookups, Discogs, TCGplayer

items.title: Buying a duplicate at a shop or show
items.problem: At a convention, record store or flea market, collectors cannot remember whether they already own a particular issue, pressing or variant and buy it again.
items.who: Comic, vinyl, trading card and coin collectors
items.workaround: Photos on phone, want lists on paper, collection apps

items.title: Tracking a want list across marketplaces
items.problem: The specific card or figure a collector needs shows up on eBay, Mercari or a forum at a good price and is gone before they see it.
items.workaround: eBay saved searches, checking multiple sites daily

items.title: Cataloguing a large collection takes forever
items.problem: Entering hundreds of items one by one into a database is so tedious that most collectors never finish, leaving them with no record for insurance.
items.workaround: Barcode-scanning apps, spreadsheets, giving up

items.title: Building and tracking a deck for card games
items.problem: Players of Magic, Pokemon or Lorcana lose track of which cards are in which deck and which are loose, so building a new deck means dismantling another.
items.workaround: Moxfield, Archidekt, deck boxes with labels

items.title: Storing and finding physical items later
items.problem: Collectors know they own an item but cannot find which box, binder or shelf it is in without emptying the closet.
items.who: Collectors who store items in bins and binders
items.workaround: Labels, memory, photos of box contents

items.title: Tracking model kit and miniature backlog
items.problem: Miniature painters and model builders accumulate a 'pile of shame' of unbuilt kits and forget which paints they need for which project.
items.who: Warhammer painters, Gundam and scale model builders
items.workaround: Spreadsheets, photos, guilt

items.title: Remembering paint recipes for miniatures
items.problem: Painters cannot reproduce a color scheme on the next batch of miniatures months later because the layered paint recipe was never written down.
items.workaround: Notebooks, photos, paint-recipe apps

items.title: Balancing hobby time across several hobbies
items.problem: People with multiple hobbies feel they neglect all of them, cannot tell how much time each got this month, and lose momentum in the ones they skipped.
items.who: Adults juggling several hobbies with work and family
items.workaround: Calendar blocks, habit trackers

items.title: Hobby spending creeping out of control
items.problem: Small purchases of yarn, games, plants or supplies add up unnoticed, and people are shocked at the total when they finally look at the bank statement.
items.workaround: Budgeting apps, self-imposed 'no buy' months

items.title: Finding a local hobby group or club
items.problem: Newcomers to a hobby or a city cannot easily find the local knitting circle, board game meetup or garden club, and Meetup listings are often dead.
items.who: People new to a hobby or area
items.workaround: Facebook groups, library notice boards, asking at shops

items.title: Documenting progress to see improvement
items.problem: Hobbyists cannot see how much better their painting, playing or crafting has gotten because early work is not photographed or dated, so they feel stuck.
items.workaround: Camera roll, Instagram accounts
